item.title: Ole Miss defense takes charge, shuts down Missouri's high-powered rushing attack in 31-3 win
item.description: Ole Miss held Missouri to just 39 rushing yards as Pete Golding's defense completely smothered Austin Simmons and the No. 13 Tigers in a rout.
item.content:encoded:
Despite his defensive background, Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding was starting to field some uncomfortable questions about his side of the ball.

That tends to happen when you give up 52 points like the Rebels did three weeks ago against Florida.

What a difference 21 days makes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Ole Miss completely smothered one of the best offenses in the SEC en route to a 31-3 drubbing over number 13 Missouri.

The Tigers came into today's matchup boasting a top-ten rushing attack and one of the nation's top quarterbacks in Austin Simmons, though you wouldn't have been able to tell after watching this game.

Give all the credit to Golding and the Rebels' defense, as the team held Mizzou to 39 yards rushing and harrassed Simmons all game.

The senior signal caller looked uncomfortable for virtually the entire game, throwing for 340 yards but needing nearly 50 attempts to do so.

LANE KIFFIN CAUGHT LYING ABOUT LSU-OLE MISS SERIES WHILE COMPLAINING ABOUT NINE-GAME SEC SCHEDULE

On the other side of the ball, Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss wasn't perfect but came through when the Rebs needed him, tossing three scores and adding another on the ground.

It was the Ole Miss rushing attack that really torched the Tigers' run defense.

The Rebels racked up 257 yards on the ground in large part because of the efforts of Kewan Lacy and backup Makhi Frazier.

Missouri looked as though they were heading for a potential College Football Playoff berth, but a blowout loss against the Rebels changes the calculus of things.

Meanwhile, Ole Miss is right back on track with all of their goals still in front of them.

The Rebels will go on the road to play a reeling Texas Longhorns team, but things don't get much easier in terms of a path to an SEC Championship and beyond.

Ole Miss will face a November stretch that includes Georgia, Oklahoma and Mississippi State.

The Tigers, on the other hand, will travel to Fayetteville to take on Arkansas, which could be just what the doctor ordered.

item.title: Unranked Auburn upsets top-ranked Georgia with walk-off field goal, marking wild feat not seen in 36 years
item.description: Kirby Smart's Bulldogs blew a 14-0 lead at home as Auburn's Alex McPherson drilled a 34-yard field goal to seal the shocking 27-24 upset win.
item.content:encoded:
Being ranked No. 1 in the country might actually be a curse.

For the first time since 1990, the No. 1 team in the nation lost to an unranked opponent in consecutive weeks after Georgia fell at home to Auburn, 27-24.

Georgia had defeated 53 consecutive unranked opponents.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It looked like all Georgia early, as they got out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. But the Dogs would not score on their next five drives, punting three times, missing a field goal and throwing a pick. The Tigers used that all to their advantage and scored 24 unanswered points to put Georgia on upset alert.

The Bulldogs entered the fourth quarter down 10, but an early field goal cut the deficit, and they were able to force two Auburn punts. After the second, they embarked on a 13-play, 94-yard touchdown drive to tie the game.

Auburn was stuffed and had to punt the ball away for a third consecutive drive, giving Georgia the ball at its own 39 with over a minute to go and all the momentum. They got a gift with a defensive pass interference on the first play.

But suddenly, all that momentum shifted.

On the next play, Gunnar Stockton lost a fumble, giving Auburn and all three of its timeouts the ball with 58 seconds at its own 44.

OHIO STATE SNAPS INDIANA'S 22-GAME WINNING STREAK, HANDS REIGNING CHAMPS FIRST LOSS SINCE 2024 IN THRILLER

The Tigers got 22 yards on three straight carries and then drew a roughing the passer penalty, putting themselves in chip-shot range.

Alex McPherson came on for a 34-yard field goal, and he drilled it to complete the upset.

Texas lost the Red River Rivalry to Oklahoma last week, causing it to drop all the way to No. 7, in case you are wondering how far Georgia may fall.

This is also Georgia's first unranked opponent loss at home under Kirby Smart since 2019.

Georgia, now 5-1, had taken the top spot after it defeated Alabama last week in a dogfight, but the spot is now up for grabs for squads like No. 2 Notre Dame, No. 3 Miami and No. 4 Ohio State.

The Bulldogs will be off next week before returning on Halloween to face Florida, which upset Texas in Austin earlier Saturday. Auburn, meanwhile, will host No. 22 LSU next week.

item.title: Limoges Town Hall 'largely lost' after far-left rioters set historic building on fire amid French unrest
item.description: Rioters set fire to the historic Limoges Town Hall, collapsing its roof and destroying much of the landmark as France's protests rage on.
item.content:encoded:
A historic building in the French town of Limoges, about three hours south of Paris, has been "largely lost" after it was set on fire by rioters as demonstrations continue across France.

The Limoges Town Hall was built in 1883, and was made a historic landmark in 1975.

"The roof has collapsed onto lower floors, except the west wing, and two-thirds of the exterior has already disappeared," the local prefect, Maurice Barate, told the AFP news agency.

MASSIVE FIRE DESTROYS 400-YEAR-OLD FOOD MARKET, LEAVING HISTORIC LANDMARK IN RUINS

Barate called it "a deliberate act by hooligans," adding that it was a "catastrophe for heritage." 

The destruction came as far-left anti-government protests and violent clashes entered their fourth week in the European country over the cost of living.

On Saturday, outgoing President Emmanuel Macron wrote on social media: "There is no place for violence in our republic."

FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION

"Those who have broken, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished," he added translated from French. "To the law enforcement forces, guarantors of the right to demonstrate, I express the support of the Nation. We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who seek only to bring down our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so."

Macron leaves office in six months.

GRETA THUNBERG JOINS MASSIVE FRENCH STUDENT PROTESTS AS CARS BURN, POLICE FIRE TEAR GAS

Around 400 people were arrested on Saturday, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, as more than a half million people took part in more than 100 marches across the country.

Masked groups also attempted to break into city halls in Lille and Calais and a police station in Brest, the interior minister reported, along with violence in Rennes, Toulouse, Montpellier and Grenoble, among other cities.

BEHIND FRANCE'S STUDENT RIOTS: COMMUNISTS, UNIONS AND A GLOBAL PROPAGANDA NETWORK

Nuñez blamed the unrest on "extremely violent, radical far-left groups."

While many of the protests were without violence, many have descended into riots. Police used tear gas and water cannons on Saturday to disperse violent groups in Paris, where people wearing hoods and masks threw fireworks and other objects at officers in the Place de la République.

item.title: Conor Kennedy, RFK Jr's son, celebrates wedding with Brazilian pop star in gorgeous setting
item.description: In Rio de Janeiro, Conor Kennedy and Giulia Be celebrated their wedding across three days, including a blessing at Christ the Redeemer and a ceremony at a historic 1808 church.
item.content:encoded:
Rio de Janeiro’s beaches, mountaintops and historic streets were among the scenes of the wedding celebration of Conor Kennedy and Brazilian pop star Giulia Bourguignon Marinho earlier this month — with plenty of images circulating across social media in recent days. 

Conor Kennedy is a son of Robert F. Kennedy Jr., secretary of Health & Human Services in the Trump administration. 

The three-day wedding celebration, which kicked off Oct. 8, included a blessing at the iconic Christ the Redeemer statue, a ceremony at the downtown church Igreja Nossa Senhora do Carmo da Antiga Sé and a reception at a historic mansion in Jardim Botânico, according to reports.

The couple officially married in a private civil ceremony in Los Angeles in March, Vogue reported.

FANS SWARM JFK JR. SITES IN MAJOR CITY AS HIT SERIES ‘LOVE STORY’ TRIGGERS TOURISM FRENZY

"We wanted to celebrate not just the wedding, but also Rio de Janeiro, the city we love," Marinho, who is professionally known as Giulia Be, told the outlet. 

"Being there, overlooking Rio, with our family was one of those moments I’ll never forget."

Earlier this year, Marinho told Brazilian outlet Globo she saw it as "the only chance to bring all of [Kennedy's] friends and all of his family to Brazil," and she "wanted to show them a good time."

She recalled that she told her then-fiancé, "'My love, I love you, but I’m not getting married in Massachusetts.'"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The church where the couple's ceremony was held, commonly called the Antiga Sé, sits in Rio’s historic center. 

It dates back to 1808, when, after the Portuguese royal court arrived in Brazil, it served as their royal chapel and cathedral.

Nearby Praça XV de Novembro is a historic square that hosts a Saturday flea market, where shoppers browse antiques, records and clothes, according to The New York Times. 

The area also offers visitors proximity to other historic sites and waterfront views.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The festivities reportedly began with a welcome party in the hills of Alto da Boa Vista. 

The next day, guests joined the couple for beach volleyball on Ipanema before attending the blessing at Christ the Redeemer, atop Corcovado Mountain.

The statue sits within Tijuca National Park, where visitors can take in views across the city.

The reception took place at Instituto Brando Barbosa in the neighborhood of Jardim Botânico, which is home to the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden, a public attraction known for its plant collection and historic grounds.

Conor Kennedy is a grandson of the late Sen. Robert F. Kennedy, President John F. Kennedy's brother.

Vogue noted that Marinho's Calvin Klein slip dress for the wedding blessing evoked the understated elegance of Carolyn Bessette Kennedy, Conor Kennedy’s late aunt by marriage.

RFK Jr. shared family photos from the festivities on social media. Pictures showed the wedding party beneath the Christ the Redeemer statue; his wife, Cheryl Hines, pictured alongside samba dancers; and the newly married couple checking their phones for updates on the Seminoles-Cardinals game.

In a response on Instagram, his new daughter-in-law commented, "Love you, Bobby."

The bride added, "It made me so happy seeing all of you enjoying my hometown."

item.title: Child among 2 killed after vehicle drives onto soccer field at Kansas sports complex
item.description: A child and an adult were killed after a vehicle drove onto a soccer field at a Wichita sports complex. Police said the driver was taken into custody
item.content:encoded:
Two people, including a child, were killed, and several others injured Saturday when a vehicle drove onto a soccer field at a sports complex in Wichita, Kansas.

The driver was taken into custody following the incident at Stryker Sports Complex, Wichita Police Capt. Aaron Moses said in a news briefing.

Sedgwick County emergency dispatchers began receiving multiple calls about the incident around 3:25 p.m., Moses said. 

Police and emergency crews responded to the complex, where two people were pronounced dead and several others were transported to area hospitals.

FORMER TV ANCHOR WHO PLEADED GUILTY TO KILLING MOTHER LAST HALLOWEEN GETS LIFE SENTENCE

The victims included a child and an adult, who have not been identified. 

Two juveniles were inside the vehicle at the time of the incident, Moses said. The vehicle remained at the scene, and police said the driver posed no additional ongoing threat to the public.

"This is a tragedy," Moses said.

The Kansas State High School Activities Association (KSHSAA) suspended play at its inaugural girls flag football state championship following the incident, which occurred on an adjacent field at Stryker Sports Complex.

LOYAL DOG FETCHES POLICE TO HELP OWNER WHO FELL AT KANSAS HOME

The association said games would not resume this weekend and that updated game times would be announced later.

Authorities have not confirmed whether the driver acted intentionally.

The Sedgwick County Sheriff's Office, Bel Aire Police Department, Kansas Highway Patrol, Wichita Fire Department and Sedgwick County Emergency Medical Services were among the agencies responding to the scene.

Police said the investigation remains in its early stages and another briefing is expected Saturday evening.

Officials asked anyone with video footage of the incident to submit it to authorities.

This is a developing story; check back later for updates.

item.title: Ohio State shatters Indiana’s 22-game winning streak, but questions linger about Julian Sayin's health
item.description: Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith scored the game-winning touchdown after admitting he ran the wrong route, ending Indiana's 22-game winning streak.
item.content:encoded:
BLOOMINGTON, IN - The biggest home game in Indiana history was ruined by Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, and a Hoosiers foot that was just out of bounds.

For the past 14 months, the talk of college football has centered around the Hoosiers stacking up wins and a national championship.

All the while, the Buckeyes just sat quietly in the background with the best player in the sport, waiting for their turn to prove the doubters wrong after a loss at Texas earlier in the season thanks to a fourth quarter collapse.

Even though Julian Sayin did not have his most productive outing on Saturday, all he needed was his Heisman Trophy candidate Jeremiah Smith to bail him out a time or two en route to a close-shave 19-15 victory over the Hoosiers.

Plenty of times this afternoon in Bloomington, it felt as though this Ohio State team was just one play away from ending the party. But, with Josh Hoover throwing a touchdown pass with just over 10:12 remaining in the fourth quarter, we found ourselves wondering if the Buckeyes would once again blow a fourth quarter lead.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S CHAOS ERA IS HERE: TEXAS RALLIES, OREGON FALLS AND LANE KIFFIN EYES RETURN TO OLE MISS

As 1:02 was remaining in the game, the Indiana crowd bursted into cheers after Nick Marsh came down with what the Hoosiers thought would be the go-ahead touchdown catch in what would be one of the wilder endings we've seen this season.

Turns out, it was one of the crazier plays we've witnessed, but for all the wrong reasons for Indiana, as Nick Marsh immediately signaled by grabbing his helmet.

As the fireworks went off inside Memorial Stadium, the mood quickly shifted within the hearts of Hoosier fans, as Nick Marsh was ruled to be out of bounds when he caught the football, sending the Ohio State sideline into a frenzy of joy.

"We had it, but we just didn’t make it happen," Curt Cignetti said following the loss. "It's a hard one to swallow, learn from it and move on."

A 22-game winning streak for Indiana came to an end, while Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia jubilantly told assistant coaches after the game that he'd rather not watch the final play over again.

What we witnessed on this chilly day in Bloomington will go down as one of the most complicated games over the past few seasons for both teams.

INDIANA'S BATTLE AGAINST OHIO STATE AT MEMORIAL STADIUM HIGHLIGHTS HOOSIERS' STRONG COMMITMENT TO THE MILITARY

Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin will at the very least be out a "couple of weeks", according to head coach Ryan Day following the game, after suffering a shoulder injury during the fourth quarter that saw him return to the sidelines wearing a sling.

Ohio State does have a bye next week, before a trip to USC in late October.

Everything was starting to come up roses for the defending national champions during a frantic fourth quarter, which also saw Jeremiah Smith give the Buckeyes the eventual game-winning touchdown.

"I actually ran the wrong route," Smith said postgame. But, Julian (Sayin) trusted me and I made the play."

The pageantry of college football was on display for the few days leading up to this top-five showdown in Bloomington, as fans flocked to town in hopes of seeing Indiana extend its winning streak to 23 games.

But, the heartbreak would come sneaking around the bend over what might be the wildest 20 seconds of recent Big Ten memory, thanks to the insane final few minutes.

NICK SABAN AND TIM TEBOW GIVE THEIR THOUGHTS ON EXPANDING THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF TO 24 TEAMS

Is this the defining game for an Ohio State football team that has all the potential to be inside Lucas Oil Stadium at regular season's end for a Big Ten title game?

Absolutely, but they'll have to get through the next month without a starting quarterback who nearly cost them the game on multiple occasions on Saturday.

In what was actually an uneventful game for nearly three full quarters, each squad decided to save their best theatrics until the final minutes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

On one hand, Indiana has a ways to go on the offensive side of the ball, even with Josh Hoover slinging it. It's no secret that this unit is not fundamentally the same as we witnessed last season, but that doesn’t mean Curt Cignetti's squad can't put itself in a position to hoist the Big Ten trophy once again.

But, the Hoosiers will need more out of their starting quarterback, along with a group of wide receivers who found themselves looking over their heads numerous times against the Buckeyes.

Who knows, maybe they put it all together, but judging by what we witnessed on Saturday, there are plenty of things to fix if they are going to make another CFP run.

For the Big Ten, nobody can deny the drama created in the buildup to this one, with so much on the line in terms of postseason placement.

A loss would not have destroyed the Buckeyes chances at making the postseason, though the same cannot be said for their week-two opponent in the Texas Longhorns after their loss to Florida.

Now, though, with a win on the road in Bloomington in front of a crowd that was foaming at the mouth for another win over the Buckeyes, this Ohio State team will have to endure at least the next few weeks of the season without Julian Sayin.

item.title: Ex-wrestler Pac's sudden death cause revealed by Cook County Medical Examiner's Office
item.description: Benjamin Satterley, known as Pac, died of bronchial asthma at 40, just one day after competing for the AEW National Championship at All Out.
item.content:encoded:
Former wrestling star Pac, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, died of bronchial asthma late last month, the California Post said, citing the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office.

Pac was 40 years old when All Elite Wrestling (AEW) announced his death.

"All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac," the company said. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans."

He challenged Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out, which occurred just one day before his death.

Pac was found dead in a rental car the next day outside of a CAVA outside of Chicago, where that bout occurred. Officers saw his phone's GPS guiding him to O'Hare airport.

PRO WRESTLER TAKING HIS SHOT AT RUNNING HIS OWN INDEPENDENT SHOW: 'LET'S JUST TAKE IT UP A NOTCH'

Pac was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion.

Before wrestling in AEW, he was with WWE and known as Adrian Neville.

Satterley was a two-time cruiserweight champion, an NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion.

item.title: Bears to start Caleb Williams vs Falcons after missing three games with hamstring injury
item.description: Caleb Williams is set to return to the Chicago Bears' starting lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing three games with a hamstring injury.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly a month after being carted off the field, Caleb Williams is set to return.

The Chicago Bears' star quarterback will return to the starting lineup after missing three games due to a hamstring injury, barring any complications during pregame warmups, OutKick confirmed. ESPN first reported Williams' return.

When Williams went down against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, Bears fans feared the worst as he grabbed the back of his leg. The 24-year-old was carted off the field in the rain, but it appeared the rain cloud would hang over the Bears much longer than that Sunday.

Instead, Williams is set to return against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. The Bears went 2-1 without Williams.

Williams made it through a full week of practice without any setbacks but told reporters on Thursday that he wasn't sure whether he would start against Atlanta. Williams refused to disclose the grade of his hamstring injury but called it "pretty serious."

The Bears started Case Keenum against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3 and won 27-7. The following week, Tyson Bagent started against the New York Jets, and the Bears won 23-12.

However, last week, the tide turned as the Green Bay Packers demolished the Bears, winning 31-7. Bagent started the game, but Keenum entered in the fourth quarter.

The Bears are 3-2, leaving them tied for second in the NFC North with the Detroit Lions and the Packers, who are also 3-2. The Vikings lead the division at 5-0, and the Bears hope Williams' return can help close that gap.

item.title: Eagles' Jalen Hurts placed on injured reserve after superficial blood clot found in his calf area
item.description: Jalen Hurts has landed on injured reserve after a superficial blood clot in his calf shifted, forcing the Philadelphia Eagles to turn to Tanner McKee.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles have placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after he was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. Hurts will now miss a minimum of four games.

The Eagles released a statement Thursday about the medical condition of their quarterback in announcing his looming absence, saying Hurts had been receiving treatment for nearly a week and even flew to and from London with it.

Hurts played in the team’s London game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and practiced in full on Wednesday, one day before the team announced he would not play Sunday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the (Los Angeles) Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report," the team said in its statement earlier this week.

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team’s flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.

"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter.

FORMER NFL TEAM DOCTOR ADDRESSES JALEN HURTS' BLOOD CLOT AS QB'S SEASON HINGES ON ONE KEY WORD

"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the (Carolina) Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

Hurts will miss games against the Panthers and each of the Eagles’ three NFC East rivals. He will be eligible to return in Week 11 against the Pittsburgh Steelers (the Birds have a Week 10 bye, which is when Hurts would initially be able to come back).

Blood clots can be dangerous because they may block blood flow to vital organs, causing a pulmonary embolism, stroke or heart attack. They can also damage tissue or be fatal if they form or travel without prompt treatment.

Tanner McKee, a third-year veteran, is Philadelphia's backup and is now in line to start against the Panthers. McKee has started two games in his career and the team has lost one and won the other.

The struggling Eagles have already been without DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley.

OutKick's Armando Salguero contributed to this report.

item.title: Texas blows 14-point lead, Arch Manning experiences first home loss as questions mount in Austin
item.description: Florida Gators stun Texas Longhorns with a 27-24 comeback win as Arch Manning struggles and Steve Sarkisian faces a must-win game against Ole Miss.
item.content:encoded:
It had the makings of another classic home win at Darrell K. Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium.

The Longhorns were up 17-3 after Ryan Niblett returned a punt for a touchdown to give the Horns a two-score lead midway through the second quarter while their opponent, the Florida Gators, looked hapless.

Then something flipped.

TEXAS LONGHORNS FAVORED BY 11.5 OVER FLORIDA GATORS DESPITE BACK-TO-BACK STRUGGLES IN SEC FOOTBALL

The Gators buckled down, adopting the hard-nosed mentality that head coach Jon Sumrall has been trying to impart on them since their blowout loss to Missouri two weeks ago, and outscored Texas 24-7 over the final two and a half quarters to nab a signature win.

Florida could have easily folded, especially given the two-game losing streak they came in on, coupled with the loss of starting quarterback Aaron Philo and top wideout Vernell Brown III.

Instead, the Gators turned to Tramell Jones, making his first collegiate start in a venue that has not been kind to opposing teams or quarterbacks.

Jones turned in a yeoman's effort, going 22-35 for 155 passing yards and two touchdowns while also keeping the Longhorn defense honest with his legs.

Running back Jadan Baugh started to look like his old self as well (25 carries for 91 yards and a score), which certainly helped Florida and Jones by extension.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

For Texas, this loss leaves a team that was a national championship favorite just two weeks ago with a lot of tough questions.

Starting with their quarterback, Arch Manning once again looked less than adequate for large stretches of the game.

Outside of a massive 62-yard pass on 4th and 7 late in the game, Manning had just over 100 yards through the air.

Give some credit to Florida's defensive line for harassing the junior signal caller for much of the day, but the Gators' pass defense has ranked in the 100s in most statistical categories and was supposed to represent a "get right" opportunity for Manning.

Instead, the beleaguered quarterback continues to slide down mock draft boards as the season matures.

UNRANKED OKLAHOMA KNOCKS OFF NO. 1 TEXAS IN WALK-OFF FASHION AFTER ARCH MANNING'S ROUGH 4TH QUARTER

For as bad as things look for Manning's future, it might look worse for Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian.

Another loss would almost certainly mean the end of the Longhorns' College Football Playoff hopes, and missing the postseason tournament two years in a row would be unacceptable for a team as talented as Texas.

Many pundits were ready to put Sarkisian on the hot seat to start the season, and if he doesn't turn things around in a hurry in Austin, he could very well be on his way out.

All the pieces were in place for the Longhorns to make a run at the title this fall, but a loss today puts everything on life support.

It doesn't get any easier, either, as Texas will welcome a top-ten Ole Miss team to DKR next week.

With coach and quarterback both under fire, the pressure could prove to be too much.

From number one in the land to crushed dreams in 14 days. College football can be so cruel.

item.title: Dream and Valkyries leave court for national anthem, return seconds later at WNBA Finals
item.description: The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries both left the court before the national anthem ahead of WNBA Finals Game 1, returning seconds later.
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO – The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries both left the court before the national anthem ahead of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday at Chase Center.

And they were back within seconds of it ending.

Both teams were on the floor beforehand, warming up for the game, then disappeared for roughly the two minutes it took to perform the "Star-Spangled Banner." Almost immediately after the singer concluded, both teams jogged back onto the floor.

Guess that's just part of the pregame routine.

WNBA FINALS: ANGEL REESE HEADLINES CHAMPIONSHIP SHOWDOWN AS LEAGUE SEEKS TO DRAW VIEWERS WITHOUT CAITLIN CLARK

In its Aug. 2, 2020, game notes, Atlanta included messaging from the WNBA players' union explaining anthem protests. The statement said "the anthem does not represent freedom, justice and liberty for all Americans" and indicated that protests would continue in different forms.

That statement was made six years ago, during the 2020 WNBA season. The reasons for Atlanta's and Golden State's absences Saturday were not immediately clear.

But the timing was. If this was about pregame preparation, what required both teams to be off the floor for those two minutes?

LONG LIST OF EMBARRASSING WNBA INCIDENTS IS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN SPORTS LEAGUES MADE POLITICS THEIR PRIMARY FOCUS

And watching an Angel Reese team miss the anthem brought back a familiar scene.

I was in Albany, New York, for LSU's Elite Eight game against Iowa in 2024. Caitlin Clark and her Hawkeyes teammates stood together, holding hands during the national anthem. Reese and the Tigers were off the floor.

After the game, I asked LSU coach Kim Mulkey whether that was a conscious decision on her part.

"Honestly, I don't even know when the anthem was played," Mulkey told me.

She explained that LSU's routine involved leaving the court at the 12-minute mark before tipoff to handle its pregame preparations. She said the absence was not intentional.

"I'm sorry, listen, that's nothing intentionally done," Mulkey said.

That was Mulkey's explanation in 2024. My question then, and the one that comes to mind again now, is why being present for the anthem can't be part of the routine.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Taking a couple of minutes to show some appreciation for the country where you're playing for a championship is a pretty reasonable expectation.

And if your pregame routine requires leaving the court for the national anthem, it's time for a new routine.

OutKick reached out the WNBA, Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries for comment but none immediately responded to request for comment.

item.title: Ohio State snaps Indiana's 22-game winning streak, hands reigning champs first loss since 2024 in thriller
item.description: Jeremiah Smith's leaping 38-yard touchdown grab and Julian Sayin's gutsy fourth-down calls powered Ohio State in it's thrilling win over Indiana.
item.content:encoded:
For the first time since December 2024, Indiana has lost a football game.

No. 4 Ohio State snapped Indiana's 22-game winning streak, beating No. 5 Indiana 19-15 despite losing star quarterback Julian Sayin to an injury on Saturday afternoon at Memorial Stadium. It was Indiana's first home loss in 19 games.

Heisman frontrunner Jeremiah Smith scored a touchdown in the fourth quarter with a spectacular catch, and Ohio State's defense repeatedly stood tall during the fourth quarter, holding the reigning national champions at bay.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Ohio State bookended the first-half scoring. Julian Sayin came out firing, quickly driving the Buckeyes into Indiana territory before the Hoosiers' defense stood tall and forced a field goal. On the final possession of the first half, Sayin drove the Buckeyes into a goal-to-go situation.

The Hoosiers' defense shut Ohio State down on the first three plays, but Ryan Day decided to go for it. Day's gamble paid off, as Sayin found a wide-open Bo Jackson in the flat for a touchdown, putting Ohio State up 10-7.

Indiana's lone touchdown in the first half came after a Sayin interception. The Buckeyes quarterback's pass was intercepted deep in Ohio State territory, and two plays later, Hoosiers running back Turbo Richard scored on a 7-yard touchdown run.

Indiana once again drove into Ohio State territory and seemed primed to score, but kicker Nico Radicic's 32-yard field goal clanged off the upright.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Down 10-7 at halftime, Indiana trailed at home at the break for the first time under Curt Cignetti.

Ohio State got the ball first in the third quarter and, as it did in the first quarter, opened the half with a field goal to extend its lead to 13-7.

After Ohio State's field goal, the teams traded turnovers. With Indiana in Ohio State territory, Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover was crushed from behind by Ohio State defender Jaylen McClain on fourth-and-4, resulting in a sack and a turnover on downs.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

However, the Buckeyes couldn't capitalize, as Sayin threw a deep pass to Jeremiah Smith that was intercepted by defensive back Amare Ferrell, his second interception of the day.

After the big hit on the previous drive, Hoover remained in the game but appeared to be playing through an injury. Despite that, Indiana was able to drive the ball into Buckeye territory again, but the Hoosiers were unable to capitalize. Radicic attempted a career-long 55-yard field goal, but it fell short, keeping Ohio State ahead 13-7.

In the fourth quarter, Smith, the aforementioned Heisman frontrunner, made his presence felt. On fourth-and-1 from the Indiana 38, Sayin launched a play-action pass toward the end zone, and Smith leaped over everyone else to haul it in for a 38-yard touchdown that put Ohio State up 19-7. The Buckeyes went for a two-point conversion but failed to convert.

Indiana promptly responded with a touchdown of its own , as wide receiver Nick Marsh hauled in a 19-yard touchdown pass to cut Ohio State's lead to 19-13. Unlike Ohio State, Indiana went for two and converted, as Hoover found Richard in the flat to cut the deficit to 19-15.

Ohio State looked to be mounting a response as it drove into Indiana territory, but Hoosiers defensive end Mario Landino hammered Sayin for an 18-yard sack and knocked him out of the game.

The Buckeyes were forced to turn to freshman quarterback Luke Fahey. With Fahey in the game, the Hoosiers' defense forced a punt to get the ball back to Hoover, giving Indiana a chance to take the lead with just over five minutes left in the fourth quarter. Yet, Indiana couldn't do anything with it and punted the ball right back. With Sayin on the sideline in a sling, Ohio State's fate was in Fahey's hands.

The Hoosiers' defense smelled blood and forced a three-and-out to once again give their offense another shot with just over three minutes left in the game.

For a brief moment, it looked like Indiana had scored the game-winning touchdown. On fourth down, Hoover took a shot for Marsh, but Marsh caught the ball out of bounds, sealing Ohio State’s 19-15 win.

item.title: Man shot and killed inside New York City subway station in Midtown Manhattan: NYPD
item.description: A man was fatally shot at a New York City subway station in Midtown Manhattan as the NYPD says no arrests have been made in the ongoing probe.
item.content:encoded:
A man was shot and killed in the New York City subway on Saturday afternoon, police confirmed to Fox News Digital.

The shooting happened at the 53rd Street and 7th Avenue station in busy Midtown Manhattan just after noon, according to the NYPD.

Hassen Pinchback from Orlando, Florida, told Fox News Digital he witnessed the incident and that everyone started running after hearing gunshots. 

"It was like a stampede," he said.

HERO DAD WHO TOOK DOWN OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTER IDENTIFIED ALONG WITH TEACHER, STUDENT BOTH KILLED IN ATTACK

"When the train doors opened, that’s when you heard pop pop pop," Pinchback said, adding that a female bystander was doing chest compressions on the victim before police arrived, telling him to ‘Hang in there.’"

Another witness from Washington state who gave the last name of "Miller," said she and her daughter heard about five shots while sitting inside the subway car with the doors open and her daughter went outside, and the shooter looked right at her before he continued shooting.

"I just started praying. I’m a very strong Christian," she said. "Jesus saved us. 100%."

JUDGE SENTENCES NEW YORK HIGH SCHOOL SENIOR WHO SET HOMELESS MAN ON FIRE ON SUBWAY

She said her daughter was able to motion to a conductor on another subway train that there was a shooter and that he called 911.

The victim was rushed to a hospital in critical condition where he later died of his injuries.

PENN STATION STABBING VICTIM SLAMS MAMDANI, DA BRAGG FOR SUSPECT BEING FREE ON STREETS

No arrests have been made, and the investigation is ongoing, the NYPD told Fox News Digital.

Later Saturday, the NYPD released images of the suspect, writing, "an unidentified individual approached an unidentified male on the northbound E train platform at the 53 Street/7 Avenue subway station in the confines of the Midtown North Precinct/Transit District 1, displayed a firearm and discharged it, striking the victim once in the chest. The individual fled the location on foot, traveling northbound on 7 Avenue." 

The grainy photos showed the suspect wearing a red hoodie and red pants, black puffy vest and a black face mask. 

"Anyone with information regarding this incident is urged to call the NYPD's Crime Stoppers Hotline at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477), or for Spanish, 1-888-57-PISTA (74782). The public may also submit tips online at Crime Stoppers website or via X @NYPDTips," the department added. 

PIX11 reported that the shooting stemmed from an argument that broke out between the shooter and the victim.

item.title: Cornell defense fights to boot Letitia James from fraternity probe, warning she cannot be fair to client
item.description: Letitia James' appointment as special prosecutor in the Cornell University fraternity sexual assault case faces a legal challenge from the defense.
item.content:encoded:
The defense attorney for a Cornell University fraternity member named in a civil sexual assault lawsuit is asking a judge to invalidate the appointment of New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor.

Speaking on "Saturday in America," attorney Andrew Miltenberg, who represents Cornell student Gillio Lopes, argued that the case has become a "cultural battleground" and that James’ public statements supporting the accuser compromised her ability to conduct an impartial investigation.

"I do not believe she can be fair. Had she made a statement that was empathetic or compassionate towards a victim, that's fine. I don't think that person can become a neutral investigator or prosecutor," Miltenberg said.

ATTORNEY FOR FORMER CORNELL FRATERNITY MEMBER WANTS AG JAMES OFF CASE OVER POST SUPPORTING ACCUSER

Before her appointment, James expressed support for Doe in a Sept. 28 post on X.

"What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. I'm holding her in my heart and in my prayers," James wrote. "To her, and to all survivors: you're not alone. We stand with you."

Miltenberg told host Kayleigh McEnany, "We welcome an investigation, just not her, and I don't know how anyone could think at this point that she could be fair."

CORNELL SEXUAL ASSAULT CASE REVIVES SCRUTINY OF A LITTLE-KNOWN NEW YORK LAW ON INTOXICATED VICTIMS

On Oct. 19, 2024, Jane Doe attended a party at Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity house. Weeks later, she filed a report with Cornell University Police detailing the alleged incident. Campus police investigated and submitted Doe's six-page voluntary sworn statement to the Tompkins County District Attorney's Office.

Prosecutors declined to pursue charges at the time, concluding that the evidence presented did not meet the threshold for criminal charges under New York law.

In the civil complaint cited on air, Doe alleged that Lopes and another defendant placed her on a bed before two men had nonconsensual sex with her. Miltenberg disputed that account, calling it "not true."

INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM

Miltenberg points to text messages Doe allegedly sent the day after the party, which he maintains show the encounters were consensual and contradict the allegations in her lawsuit.

"I understand that perceptions shift and memories shift after a period of time, but her initial statements, her initial texts, her initial testimony with respect to the police, all was very clear about how she viewed this situation," Miltenberg said.

While acknowledging that "post-traumatic stress memory repression is a real thing," Miltenberg maintained that the earliest records contradict the allegations in Doe's lawsuit.

TISH JAMES CONFRONTED ON CAMERA OVER TRUMP'S ACCUSATION OF BIAS IN CORNELL RAPE CASE

The case drew the attention of New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who appointed James as special prosecutor. In her order, Hochul cited concerns raised by Doe and the public that the alleged incident could not be investigated locally "without conflict or bias."

LETITIA JAMES' 'FAIR' CORNELL RAPE PROBE VOW COLLIDES WITH ACCUSED AIDE'S 'QUIET' EXIT

James has rejected accusations that she prejudged the case, saying during an attorney general campaign debate that her comments supporting the alleged victim were intended to demonstrate "empathy" and insisting that "politics stops at the door" of her office.

Miltenberg and an attorney representing another defendant have filed a motion seeking to invalidate James' appointment as special prosecutor. Miltenberg said he believes the challenge has a "good chance of having her appointment voided."

WHO IS SALLY YATES? CORNELL RAPE-REVIEW PICK WAS FIRED BY TRUMP AFTER REFUSING TO DEFEND TRAVEL BAN

"I am hopeful that the judge will see it that way and will void her appointment and appoint or ask the governor to appoint someone equally as experienced, equally as interested in the facts and perhaps less personally invested in the case," he said.

Miltenberg said Lopes remains enrolled at Cornell, adding that his client is "keeping a low profile, and he is looking forward to finishing his degree as a regular college student."

Fox News Digital reached out to the New York Attorney General's Office and Doe's legal team for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Fox News Digital's Elaine Mallon contributed to this report.

item.title: West Virginia medical team backs cart into wall with injured Cincinnati player onboard

item.content:encoded:

SOCCER PLAYER GETS SMOKED BY LAWN ROLLER DURING HALFTIME WARM-UP IN WILD MOMENT CAUGHT ON CAMERA

If that's really how it goes, then this guy broke the golden rule.

Of course it was an accident — although it's a great way to thin out the opposition's roster a little bit — but Hough did not return to the game.

item.title: Former MIT scientist wins $6M defamation verdict against colleague who accused him of sexual misconduct
item.description: David Sabatini won $6 million after a jury found his colleague's sexual harassment claims were defamatory, but the fallout from MIT cost him years.
item.content:encoded:
A former Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) scientist won a legal victory this week after losing his position following sexual misconduct allegations made by a female colleague.

Dr. David Sabatini, a former MIT biology professor and prominent biomedical researcher, was awarded $6 million in damages Friday after a jury found that his former colleague, Dr. Kristin Knouse, had defamed him.

At the time of the allegations, Sabatini had led a research lab at the Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for approximately 24 years. His work focused on cell biology and its connections to neurodegenerative diseases, diabetes, aging and cancer.

FORMER CAL SOFTBALL PLAYER FILES LAWSUIT AGAINST UNIVERSITY, FEMALE EX-COACH OVER ALLEGED SEXUAL MISCONDUCT

In 2021, Sabatini lost his position at Whitehead following an internal investigation into allegations made by Dr. Kristin Knouse, a younger colleague who worked at the institute.

The pair met in 2012 and began a sexual relationship in 2018, which ended the following year, according to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital. Knouse later alleged the relationship was coerced.

AOC'S DRAMATIC RETELLING OF CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS COLLIDES WITH COMPLAINT DETAILS

According to records from the investigation, Whitehead also found that Sabatini had fostered a sexualized atmosphere in his lab. He subsequently resigned from the institute.

Following his departure from Whitehead — and amid an ongoing investigation at MIT — Sabatini filed a defamation lawsuit against Knouse, "alleging claims for defamation, tortious interference with contractual, prospective, and advantageous relations," according to court documents.

US OLYMPIC HERO NANCY HOGSHEAD WINS LEGAL BATTLE AFTER VOLLEYBALL COACH'S $250M DEFAMATION SUIT IS DISMISSED

Knouse subsequently filed a counterclaim against Sabatini, alleging sexual harassment.

Throughout the legal battle, Sabatini maintained that he had never fostered an improper atmosphere in his lab and that his relationship with Knouse was consensual.

EX-MAYOR FOUND LIABLE FOR ALLEGED SEXUAL ASSAULTS OF 7 WOMEN, ORDERED TO PAY $13M

During the trial, his attorney, Lisa Arrowood, cited text messages between the pair that she argued showed Knouse willingly participated in their relationship.

In one 2020 exchange, Knouse lamented that she was "pouring a lot of energy and emotion into a game I'm destined to lose" and wondered "if it's best for both of us to cut all but work-related ties for the foreseeable future."

FORMER UCLA GYNECOLOGIST SENTENCED AFTER PLEADING GUILTY TO SEXUALLY ASSAULTING PATIENTS AT SCHOOL

She concluded the message by writing, "But most times I feel at peace and want to do everything and anything I can to help you."

Sabatini and his legal team argued in court that the relationship was consensual. They also presented evidence they said showed that Knouse had become jealous of another woman in whom Sabatini was interested and had sought to have him fired.

HARVEY WEINSTEIN SENTENCED TO 15 YEARS IN PRISON FOR 2006 SEX CRIME IN NEW YORK

A day after a Suffolk County jury awarded him $6 million in damages, Sabatini told Fox News Digital that hearing the verdict was "overwhelming."

"It was done," Sabatini said. "We had won everything, lost nothing. It was like a complete sweep."

HOUSE BACKS MASSIE'S PUSH TO RELEASE TAXPAYER-FUNDED SEXUAL HARASSMENT SETTLEMENT RECORDS

Five years after filing his lawsuit, Sabatini emerged from the trial with a favorable verdict after the jury rejected Knouse's counterclaims, including her allegation that he had coerced her into a sexual relationship.

"The sad reality of our time is that society still has a difficult time believing women and appreciating the difficulty they encounter with men who too often control their fate," Knouse’s attorney, Ellen Zuker, said in a statement to the New York Times.

Knouse’s attorney did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Despite the legal victory, Sabatini is now attempting to pick up the pieces of his career. The allegations seeped into every aspect of his life, and many of his loved ones — including his parents, nephew and high school-aged son — began receiving threats shortly after Knouse’s claims were made public.

"Everyone who came out and tried to defend me got attacked every which way," Sabatini told Fox News Digital.

Shortly after his departure from MIT and Whitehead, Sabatini discussed a potential faculty position at New York University (NYU). But after students and faculty members protested his possible hiring in 2022, the university ultimately did not offer him a job.

Sabatini said protesters also appeared outside his parents' home, drawing his family further into the controversy.

One year later, in 2023, Sabatini landed a job at the Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry in Prague after receiving several offers from foreign countries — including China. He later opened a Boston branch of the institute, and he splits his time between Prague and the United States.

"It was a necessity," Sabatini said. "There were no options [in the United States]. So there was no choice."

Following Friday's verdict, Knouse's attorneys said they planned to appeal, while Sabatini's legal team also prepared to challenge the dismissal of his claims against the Whitehead Institute.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"I think institutions don't care about due process," Sabatini said. "They care about having a certain conclusion. And for whatever reason that one could discuss, at that time the conclusion was, ‘Get this guy out of here and make an example of him.’"

Sabatini said he hopes to rebuild his life and career following the verdict and eventually return to working primarily in the United States.

"But ultimately for me, it’s just being able to be close to my son before he goes to college," Sabatini told Fox News Digital. "That’s really number one through 100."

Fox News Digital also reached out to the Whitehead Institute and MIT for comment.

item.title: Joy Behar wants Trump back on ‘The View’ despite saying he’s ‘not long for this world’
item.description: Joy Behar invited Trump back to "The View" while claiming he's "not long for this world," prompting a sharp response from the White House team.
item.content:encoded:
"The View" co-host Joy Behar extended an unlikely invitation Friday to her longtime political foe President Donald Trump, saying she would welcome him back to the daytime talk show despite suggesting that he is "not long for this world."

Behar, who has said she wants her legacy to include helping remove Trump from office, reflected on her decades-long history with the president during an interview with New York Magazine.

"I’d love Donald Trump to take the heat," said the longtime Trump critic.

"You know Trump is not long for this world. He seems ill. He does not seem like he’s well," Behar added.

BILL MAHER REVEALS HE'S HAVING DINNER WITH TRUMP AGAIN, SAYS HE WAS 'REALLY NICE' BY TEXT

A White House spokesperson responded to Behar’s comments about Trump’s well-being in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"‘Joyless’ Behar is an extremely unlikeable, talentless hack with a poorly rated TV show who clearly suffers from a severe and incurable disease known as Trump Derangement Syndrome," the statement said.

"I lose braincells every single time I have the displeasure of hearing her speak," the spokesperson continued.

TRUMP DECLARED 'FULLY FIT' FOR ALL PRESIDENTIAL DUTIES AFTER ANNUAL PHYSICAL SHOWS 'EXCELLENT HEALTH'

Behar’s comments mark the latest instance in which "The View" co-host has publicly questioned Trump’s health.

Last month, she argued that the media does not scrutinize Trump’s health to the same degree it scrutinized former President Joe Biden’s.

Despite their bitter political divide today, Behar and Trump share a history from long before his political career.

Trump made more than a dozen appearances on "The View" before he was president and Behar even attended his wedding to Marla Maples at The Plaza Hotel in 1993.

DONALD TRUMP'S AGE IS NOT RECEIVING THE SAME 'SCRUTINY' AS BIDEN'S DID, ATLANTIC WRITER COMPLAINS

Behar said Trump’s humor has changed significantly since she knew him as a New York celebrity decades ago.

"I knew him when he was just an annoying New York figure," she said. "Back then, he had a sense of humor that was not as bizarre as it is now. Now his sense of humor is making fun of handicapped people."

"The View" co-host recalled her earlier interactions with Trump, including a time in which she compared Trump to Woody Allen after he said that he would date his daughter Ivanka if they were not related. 

"He actually thought that was funny," Behar said.

Behar has said that Trump is "much more dangerous" now than he was during his first term and recently urged Americans to call on their members of Congress to invoke the 25th Amendment against him because she believes he is "destroying the United States of America."

item.title: California diners are cutting back as costs soar — but restaurant owner reveals one trend that's booming
item.description: Happy hour business jumped from roughly 8% to nearly 30% of sales at a San Diego restaurant group as California diners hunt for cheaper meals.
item.content:encoded:
Happy hour is becoming the main event for some California diners as the state's high cost of living pushes more customers to seek out discounted meals instead of paying full price for a night out.

Chef Alex Carballo of Grand Restaurant Group told Fox News Digital that happy hour once accounted for an estimated 5% to 8% of his business. Now, that figure has climbed to nearly 30%, even as customers cut back on dining out.

"My happy hour has increased a lot, so I think people are looking for deals and looking for options," Carballo said.

The shift reflects a broader affordability squeeze across California where residents told Fox News Digital that rising costs for housing, groceries and gasoline are forcing them to rethink everyday spending. 

California has the highest overall price levels in the nation, according to 2024 data from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, with prices running roughly 11% above the national average. But affordability pressures extend far beyond the Golden State, as Americans nationwide grapple with elevated costs for housing, groceries and other everyday necessities.

NEWSOM UNDER FIRE AS CALIFORNIA GAS TAX HIKE SENDS PUMP PRICES EVEN HIGHER

Carballo said customers are visiting his restaurants less frequently, with some scaling back how often they eat out.

"They're going out three times a week, where they were coming out to see me four or five [times]. And the people that used to see three times a week, they're only coming out once," he said.

What was once a stop for drinks or appetizers before dinner is increasingly becoming the dinner itself, Carballo said.

"Now it's like, that's where they're going and they're hitting those scenes," he said.

Customers can still enjoy the same food, service and atmosphere at lower prices, Carballo said, making happy-hour deals particularly appealing.

But those discounts also create challenges for restaurant operators who are already grappling with rising expenses.

"I'm still paying the same amount for food. I'm still paying the employees. My rent didn't change. Nothing changed. Only thing I'm doing is trying to discount my product to gain people to come here," Carballo said.

AMERICANS SAY TIPPING PRACTICES 'HAVE BECOME RIDICULOUS' AS DIGITAL PROMPTS PUSH HIGHER GRATUITIES

Fox News Digital also spoke with residents in Southern California who described making financial trade-offs that extend well beyond restaurants.

Jonas, a Santa Monica resident who is planning a wedding with his fiancée, said he and his fiancée are reevaluating their budget as everyday expenses continue to add up.

"Certainly gas is expensive, rent is high, and then grocery prices are pretty high as well," Jonas said.

He estimated that he spends approximately $100 a week on groceries and said rising costs are influencing their decisions about dining out and transportation.

The couple is "eating out a little bit less," Jonas said, adding that he has also started walking to work to "save money on gas as well."

"I think that people are just seeing prices go up everywhere, and feeling like they're getting less than what they had four years ago maybe," he said. "I think everybody's really feeling that."

BELOVED RESTAURANT CHAIN DWINDLES FROM 850 LOCATIONS TO 87, BUT EXPERT SEES 'A LOT OF LIFE LEFT'

For some Californians, the financial strain has gone beyond cutting back on restaurants.

Justin, a California native from Glendora who moved to Las Vegas seven years ago, told Fox News Digital that the state's high cost of living was one of the reasons he left.

"Affordability is crazy," Justin said while visiting Los Angeles for a Rams game.

"I left seven years ago and I thought gas and you know rent was high then," he said. "Here I am seven years later and it's ... one of the reasons why I'm in Vegas now. It's just unaffordable."

Justin said many of his friends who remain in California are still struggling with housing costs.

EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE LA'S HOMELESS HELLSCAPE — UNLIKELY CRITICS BLAST DEMS AS GOP HOPEFUL TOURS SKID ROW

"90% of my friends are living with a roommate. It is really hard to live alone here," he said.

Housing remains another major affordability challenge in the Golden State. Just 19% of California households could afford the state's median-priced home of $916,750 in the second quarter of 2026, according to the California Association of Realtors.

In Venice, resident Tatiana described rising expenses across everything from gasoline to groceries and neighborhood restaurants.

"Everything is more expensive, gas is more expensive, food," she told Fox News Digital. "There's really very few affordable restaurants left on Abbot Kinney. Even our local co-op prices have gone up at least 15%. Everything costs more."

"We're not getting any breaks in California," she said.

item.title: Nick Saban and Tim Tebow give their thoughts on expanding the College Football Playoff to 24 teams
item.description: Nick Saban says there aren't 24 College Football Playoff teams that can win a title, warning bowl games and the SEC Championship Game face extinction.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday morning, before a full slate of college football games, including two Top-10 matchups (Ohio State vs Indiana and Notre Dame vs BYU), many media personalities got the chance to make their opinions known about the expansion of the College Football Playoff from 12 teams to 24. Two of the most prominent voices were former Alabama head coach, Nick Saban and former Heisman Trophy winner, Tim Tebow.

Saban, sitting down with his fellow hosts on ESPN's "College GameDay" on the campus of BYU, made a very definitive statement. "People want to see the best teams in the Playoffs. There's not 24 teams in the country that deserve to be in the playoffs," he started. "I don't think there's 24 teams in the country that can win the championship."

Saban went on to say: "Bowl games are gonna be a thing of the past."

COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF EXPANDING TO 24 TEAMS IN 2027, WITH MORE GAMES COMING TO CAMPUSES ACROSS THE COUNTRY

In my opinion, bowl games were on life support once the NCAA introduced the 12-team College Football Playoff and NIL deals. They were instantly devalued and there wasn't nearly enough incentive for players to participate in the Mom & Pop Mortgage Weedwacker Bowl (this is obviously not a real bowl, but you get the point). Why risk injury and participate in a bowl where there is virtually no upside? That's the way most players and teams view bowl games now.

Saban also mentioned, "We're gaining something but we're also giving something up. There's gonna be no SEC Championship Game now."

NICK SABAN WANTS A DIFFERENT CRITERIA FOR JUDGING WHICH TEAMS REACH THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

While Saban and the "College GameDay" crew acknowledged there are pros and cons in the expanded Playoff, it did seem like the cons outweighed the pros in Saban's mind.

As for Tebow, he made his voice heard on the SEC Network. "We changed the goal posts. Before it was about how consistent can you be throughout the season? Now it's can you just get in and get hot at the right time?," Tebow stated.

"It takes away the consistency. Before you had to focus every single week and you had to show up and you had to bring your best. Now, you have weeks where you don't have to show up."

"One of the biggest reasons why I don't like it, is because when you're looking at this game (college football), there's a few things that separate us: It's the regular season," Tebow added. "The regular season is so critical. It's so important. Now you're diluting something that was so special and it was one of the biggest differentiators from the rest of the country, and all of these other sports (college and pro)."

The proposal for expanding the College Football Playoff to 24 teams is nearly locked in, which would give teams seeded 1 through 8 a first-round bye, followed by a home game. item.title: Engelbert Humperdinck says he tied up a nurse during tuberculosis sanatorium stay after painful treatment
item.description: Engelbert Humperdinck revealed on his podcast how he tied up a nurse during his 1961 tuberculosis sanatorium stay after painful daily injections.
item.content:encoded:
Engelbert Humperdinck opened up about the time he spent in a sanatorium in 1961.

During a recent episode of his podcast, "The Engelbert Humperdinck Show," the 90-year-old British singer recalled his time at Leicester's Groby Road Hospital Sanatorium, after he was diagnosed with tuberculosis.

When speaking about the treatments he endured, he described having "to stay on your back for I don't know 8 weeks," without attempting to sit up or "do anything strenuous," in addition to getting "an injection with a needle about this big in your butt" every morning.

"There was one lady nurse who was, I don't think she liked me very much because of the injection that she gave me, she really hurt, and I used to scream at her and I used to ask for somebody else. They wouldn't give me anybody else, but this lady was very bad, and she was really hurt, and I had big blue marks," he explained.

ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK SAYS HE ‘WENT THROUGH HELL’ REJECTING 'CASTING COUCH' ADVANCES EARLY IN CAREER

After she continued to hurt him with every injection, Humperdinck thought to himself, "When I'm a little better I'm going to do something" and be a bit "mischievous" to get back at her.

"I said to my friend in the next bed, I said, 'I've got to get some rope. I get some rope,'" he said. "So we got this rope, and when the nurse came around in the morning before doctor's rounds, I got the nurse, grabbed her, tied her hands behind the back, put her in the empty bed next to us, covered her up."

He said when the doctor came by for his rounds, "he knew that I was responsible for that..but he ignored it" and "just walked straight by."

Once she was free from the bindings, the singer said he "was in trouble," but that he "never let her give me another injection."

"I said, 'I don't want her to give me,'" he said. "And they had a male nurse come and do it for me, and it was much better."

Humperdinck spent six months in the sanatorium after he started coughing up blood during a concert in Manchester. After initially receiving a diagnosis of "a bad throat infection," his mom told the doctor 'I'm not happy with that. Not when I see blood,' and demanded an X-ray.

He explained that within an hour of getting the X-ray he was told to pack his belongings as he had tuberculosis and needed to be sent to the sanatorium.

"Eight weeks later, when I became negative from this disease, my mother visited and, I said, 'Mom, is this place a great place?' I said, 'Cause you remember when you brought me in, the priest was here spent an hour with me,'" he said. "She said, 'Son he was giving you the last rites.' Apparently I had three days."

item.title: LSU stays alive in College Football Playoff race with blowout win over No 16 Mississippi State
item.description: No. 22 LSU kept their College Football Playoff hopes alive with a dominant win over No. 16 Mississippi State at home on Saturday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
For one more week, LSU remains alive in the College Football Playoff hunt.

Lane Kiffin's squad bounced back in a big way after its crushing overtime loss to Kentucky last week, beating No. 16 Mississippi State 31-0 on Saturday at Tiger Stadium. Mississippi State was without star quarterback Kamario Taylor due to a foot injury, and the Bulldogs sorely missed him.

Freshman Parker Puckett started in Taylor's stead and struggled, completing 16 of his 26 passes for 121 yards and one interception. Compounding matters for the freshman quarterback, No. 22 LSU jumped out to an early lead, leaving Puckett playing from behind the entire game.

On Mississippi State's ensuing possession, Puckett threw an interception. LSU once again marched down the field, and Leavitt found Jackson Harris for a 27-yard touchdown to put LSU up 14-0 in the first quarter.

In the second quarter, Leavitt connected with Harris again for a 17-yard touchdown to put the Tigers up 21-0. It looked like Mississippi State was going to get on the board when its offense drove into the red zone on the following possession, but the Bulldogs went for it on fourth-and-goal from the LSU 6-yard line and failed to convert.

item.title: ALDS postponement leaves Guardians ticket holders upset with altered game assignments
item.description: Cleveland Guardians fans with ALDS Game 5 tickets now face a swap to Game 4 after the rain delay, potentially missing a pennant-clinching moment.
item.content:encoded:
Some Cleveland Guardians fans got screwed by the rain in more ways than one on Friday night.

For starters, Game 4 of the American League Division Series was postponed due to weather, but not until roughly an hour after the originally scheduled first pitch, meaning fans had traveled to the game and potentially paid for parking, food and merchandise.

The postponement, ironically, came despite the Guardians' X account posting "Rain or shine" an hour before first pitch. But the mess took a turn when the Guardians announced a slight change in the tickets for the game.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Guardians said that fans with tickets for Game 4 will be able to use them for Game 5, which is now on Sunday instead of the originally planned Saturday. Fans with Game 5 tickets "do not need to take action" and can go to the ballpark on Saturday night.

That seems fine at the outset until one realizes that fans who bought tickets to Game 5 in hopes of seeing a pennant victory will not be able to do so, since they are now going to Game 4 — Cleveland is up 2-1 on the Tampa Bay Rays.

"This is an insane way to handle tickets. Tomorrow should be Game 4 and Sunday should be Game 5. Tickets should be used in that order. This is gonna cause hella problems," one user on X wrote on Friday night.

RAIN FORCES MLB TO POSTPONE GUARDIANS-RAYS ALCS GAME 4 IN CLEVELAND

"Imagine you thought you had tickets to a possible pennant-clinching win at home tomorrow night and they just casually change your tickets to Game 4. Totally ridiculous. Game is not of equal value," wrote another. "Tickets should remain assigned to their originally designated Game # in the series."

"I'd be a little annoyed if I bought what could be series ending tickets and got moved up a game," said one more.

On the flip side, if the Guardians win on Saturday, those who had tickets for what was supposed to be Friday's game could get quite lucky.

If the weather holds this time around, first pitch is at 8:00 p.m. ET.
